stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = 3x - 2\) and \(g(x) = kx + 13\), where \(k\) is a constant. In the \(xy\)-plane, the graphs of \(y = f(x)\) and \(y = g(x)\) intersect at the point \((p, q)\), where \(p + q = 10\). What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: The point \((p, q)\) is on the graph of \(f\), so \(q = 3p - 2\). With \(p + q = 10\): \(p + 3p - 2 = 10\), so \(p = 3\) and \(q = 7\).
The point \((3, 7)\) is also on the graph of \(g\): \(3k + 13 = 7\), so \(3k = -6\) and \(k = -2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(3k\), the value before dividing by 3; \(3k = -6\) gives \(k = -2\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the \(x\)-coordinate \(p\) of the intersection point, not the value of \(k\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(-k\), from a sign slip when solving \(3k + 13 = 7\); the slope must be negative for \(g\) to come down from 13 to 7.
explanation.D: Correct. The intersection point is \((3, 7)\), and \(g(3) = 7\) requires \(3k + 13 = 7\), so \(k = -2\).

verify:
p, q, k = symbols('p q k')
sol = solve([Eq(q, 3*p - 2), Eq(p + q, 10)], [p, q])
assert sol == {p: 3, q: 7}
ks = solve(Eq(k*sol[p] + 13, sol[q]), k)
assert ks == [-2]
assert value(choices[answer]) == -2
assert all(value(choices[c]) != -2 for c in choices if c != answer)
